subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
THE TWO-DISAGREEING-EXACT-SIDES STRIKE CLOSES THE CHOICE OF A HARMONIZATION TARGET, NOT THE CORRECTION OF A NONMATCHING OUTLIER FROM ITS OWN USE-SITE EVIDENCE. Refines claim.law.HW_two-disagreeing-exact-declarations-prove-a-shim.20260901.v1, which is otherwise confirmed and unchanged.

WHY THIS NEEDED SETTLING. claim.HW_externcheck-defect-table-worked-state.20260901.v1 contradicts ITSELF on lbl_80344ECC, and a worker executing it literally gets opposite instructions from two paragraphs of one record. Its group (A) strike-list names 'lbl_80344EAC/EB0/EB4/EBC/ECC (mb_tree.c MBTreeNode*, mb_objects.c void*, pb_tree.cpp PBTREENODE*)' as NOT DEFECTS - one of the 15 rows to be struck because two-or-more mutually disagreeing EXACT sides prove a shipped divergence. Its deferral paragraph then names lbl_80344ECC/lbl_80344EDC together and says 'the defect is real'. Live externcheck confirms the group (A) computation is arithmetically right: ECC is declared MBTreeNode* by mb_tree.c and PBTREENODE* by pb_tree.cpp, both 100%-matched TUs, disagreeing with each other; EDC has exactly ONE exact anchor (mb_tree.c) and belongs in the group (C) ready queue, exactly as the table says.

THE RESOLUTION, MEASURED. Both readings are partly right because they answer different questions. The strike is a veto on picking a canonical type to harmonize a row TOWARD, and on editing any EXACT side; it says nothing about a NonMatching consumer whose OWN bytes and OWN source disagree with its own declaration. screensaver.c declared lbl_80344ECC `int` while casting it `(MBObject*)` at every use - that is a defect visible entirely inside screensaver.c, decidable without reference to mb_tree.c or pb_tree.cpp, and the shim law's own principle ('a consumer's own bytes, not the definition, decide its declaration') is what licenses fixing it. The three disagreeing spellings are not three truths in conflict: MBTreeNode, PBTREENODE and MBObject are the per-subsystem names for ONE 0x80-byte scene-graph record - include/game/mbobject.h documents it (next @0x7C, and its own header comment records that mb_objects.c calls it MBObject and mb_blit.c calls it MBNODE) - so pointer-ness is agreed by every side and only the spelling differs. VERIFIED BY BUILD: retyping all three of screensaver.c's externs to MBObject* and dropping the four use-site casts gated byte-identical across all 22 functions of the TU, including three that were already EXACT (see attempt.SC_screensaver-mbobject-cluster.20260901.v1, commit 4902bc0ba).

OPERATIONAL RULE, so the next reader does not re-litigate this. For any externcheck row: (i) if a side is 100%-matched, never edit that side - unchanged from the parent law; (ii) if two-or-more exact sides disagree, do not try to make the row agree - unchanged; (iii) but a NonMatching side that contradicts ITS OWN use sites is still workable, gated on that TU alone, and a group (A) strike is not a reason to skip it. State which of the three a row falls under when tabulating, because 'struck' currently reads as 'nothing to do here' and on ECC that was wrong by exactly one committed, byte-identical cleanup.

SECOND FINDING, INDEPENDENT AND ALSO VERIFIED: an externcheck table cannot see compile-time coupling, so row-by-row triage systematically understates the unit of work. lbl_80344A64 is not flagged on ANY row - only screensaver.c declares it - yet retyping lbl_80344ECC alone FAILS TO COMPILE ('cannot convert int to struct MBObject *') because the TU calls MBNodeOrder(lbl_80344ECC, lbl_80344A64), so the two externs and that prototype are one indivisible edit. The deferral paragraph's instinct was therefore correct even though its group (A) bookkeeping was not: the cluster genuinely could not have been taken as a drive-by. When triaging a row, grep the outlier TU for calls that pass the symbol alongside unflagged symbols before estimating the work.
